subject: biology
title: Darwin's Big Idea
welcome_lead: Today you'll follow Charles Darwin to the Galapagos and uncover the four-step rule that explains every species alive.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology Natural Selection foundations — Darwin's theory, variation, competition, survival of the fittest, finch evidence.
final_note: You learned Darwin's four-step mechanism — variation, competition, survival, reproduction — and three pieces of evidence (finches, fossils, modern DNA).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Natural selection runs on 4 steps:

1) Variation exists. 2) Competition for food, mates, space.

3) The fittest survive. 4) They reproduce and pass on the helpful alleles.

Darwin saw finches on each island had different beak shapes.

Short stubby beaks crushed seeds. Long thin beaks probed insects.

Each population had adapted to its food. Same ancestor, different futures.

1) Fossils show slow change in body forms over millions of years.

2) Antibiotic resistance in bacteria — evolution we can watch this week.

3) DNA comparison — closely related species share more genes.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the correct order for natural selection?
options: Reproduction → variation → competition → survival
Variation → competition → survival of the fittest → reproduction
Mutation → extinction → survival → reproduction
Adaptation → mutation → variation → fossils

mcqs.q: What did Darwin notice about Galapagos finch beaks?
options: They were all identical
They were shaped to match the food on each island
They changed colour with the seasons
They were all imported by humans

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Humans evolved from monkeys but chimps evolved from gorillas.
Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Humans evolved from monkeys but chimps evolved from gorillas.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
No — humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor; both have evolved from it.
Humans evolved directly from chimpanzees, which is why chimps still exist as a less-evolved version.

mcqs.q: What is produced in anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
options: Lactic acid (lactate) and a small amount of ATP — no CO2 or water in this pathway.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
Anaerobic respiration produces ethanol and CO2 in humans.

mcqs.q: In what year did Darwin publish 'On the Origin of Species'?
On a windy island, insects with smaller wings are less likely to be blown out to sea and more likely to survive and breed. Over time the population has mostly small wings. This is an example of:
options: Natural selection
Selective breeding
A change made deliberately by the insects
Inheritance of an acquired characteristic

mcqs.q: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria become more common because:
options: Resistant bacteria survive treatment and reproduce.
The antibiotic teaches bacteria to resist.
Bacteria decide to become resistant.
All bacteria are resistant from the start.

mcqs.q: Which statement about variation is needed for natural selection to occur?
options: There must be heritable variation within the population.
All individuals must be genetically identical.
Variation must be caused only by the environment.
Variation must disappear each generation.

mcqs.q: Darwin's finches on different islands had differently shaped beaks suited to their food. This best supports the idea that:
options: Beak shape was selected for by the available food.
The finches chose their beak shapes.
All finches had identical beaks.
Beak shape is unrelated to survival.
